Subject: Post-demo metrics — quick clarification on QPS and p95 targets

Thanks again for the demo earlier — it was helpful to see the caching and fallback paths in action. A couple quick clarifications so we can make an internal recommendation:  

- Our target path is real-time recommendations for checkout flows (99% of traffic) plus a small async batch job for nightly personalization.
- Current production footprint (approx): steady-state ~60 reqs/sec, 95th percentile spikes up to ~700 reqs/sec for ~30-90s during promotions.
- Current P95 observed at our stack is ~180ms end-to-end for the model call (we'd like to get to ~100ms or below at peak if possible).

Questions for you:  
1) Based on those numbers, do you recommend Dedicated capacity or Hosted? Is there a hybrid configuration (reserved baseline + hosted burst) you typically propose?  
2) Any constraints we should know on cold-starts for Dedicated pools vs Hosted?  
3) If we pursue Dedicated, can you share typical lead time for reserved GPU provisioning and a rough price delta versus Hosted for our footprint?

I'll attach a CSV with a few 24-hour samples. If it's easier, we can do a short technical dive — Ana and I can join.

—Samir
Samir Patel

Subject: Re: Post-demo metrics — quick clarification on QPS and p95 targets

Samir — thanks for the detail and the sample CSV (got it). High level guidance based on what you shared:  

- Recommendation: a baseline Dedicated pool sized for your steady-state (60 qps) with Reserved capacity sized to smoothly handle mid-sized bursts, plus Hosted as an overflow for the rare extreme spikes. That hybrid gives the best cost predictability + guaranteed SLO for most calls while still preventing tail outages during promos.

- Why not pure Hosted: Hosted is simplest and elastic, but sustained 60 qps at low p95 targets tends to be more cost-effective on Dedicated, and you get tighter latency SLOs.

- Why not pure Dedicated: Dedicated autoscaling and burst-capacity help, but very short, high-magnitude spikes (like sudden promo traffic) are still where Hosted fallback is useful to avoid overprovisioning.

Quick asks to finalize a clear recommendation (I've attached an RFI with the exact fields we need):  
- Average request payload size (tokens) and typical sequence length for the recommendation model.  
- Fraction of calls that must be strictly sub-100ms versus those that can tolerate 200–300ms.
- Are you calling multiple models per request (e.g., candidate generation + rerank) or a single end-to-end model?
- Any compliance/networking constraints that would force Private (VPC) deployment?

Next steps I propose: Ben or I take a 30–45m technical deep-dive (benchmarks + deployment options) this week. I can run a short break-even calc (Dedicated reserved hours vs hosted token cost) once we have token sizes. 

Attaching: RFI_deploy_mode_questions.pdf (fields marked critical).

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,

Quick technical addendum from my side:  

- Observations on your numbers: 60 qps steady + short 700 qps spikes is a classic case for baseline Dedicated + hosted overflow. Dedicated will give you predictable P95 at the baseline; hosted fallback handles the short, elastic tail without forcing you to reserve full capacity.

- Cold starts: With Dedicated, we keep warmed workers and maintain KV cache; cold-starts are typically sub-50ms additional overhead for warmed pools. Hosted cold-start is larger for rare model swaps but generally not material for steady traffic.

- Autoscale and burst model: We recommend a reserved baseline (e.g., N GPUs tuned for your model family) + configured burst lanes (pre-warmed) for predictable promo bursts. In our experience, setting a burst buffer sized for ~200–300 qps peaks handles most promo patterns; anything beyond that routes to Hosted overflow.

- Caching & batching knobs: If your requests have a lot of repeated prefixes (e.g., same categories), prefix caching can chop 20–40% off effective qps. Continuous batching with small batch windows reduces GPU cost while keeping latency within SLOs if your p95 tolerance is >=100ms.

Proposed times for a 45m technical deep-dive (we'll bring infra + runtime leads):
- Thu 15 Oct, 10:00–10:45 PT
- Thu 15 Oct, 13:00–13:45 PT

Also attaching a quick pricing sketch for Dedicated vs Hosted for the footprint you described: redwood_dedicated_pricing_matrix.xlsx (estimates).

If you want, Marissa can run a 1-page break-even that compares monthly committed cost vs hosted expected token cost based on payload sizes.

—Ben

- Payload / tokens: median request ~120 tokens, 95th ~380 tokens. Most calls are single-model (candidate gen + lightweight rerank happens client-side for ~10% of requests).
- Hard latency requirement: ~25% of checkout calls should be sub-100ms (these are time-critical UX flows); remainder can be up to 250ms during promos.
- No compliance mandate for Private now; we may revisit once we scope PII retention.
- Promo pattern: spikes to ~700 qps for 60–120 seconds, roughly 3–4 times per week.

We can do Thu 15 Oct 10:00–10:45 PT — Ana and I will join; please send a calendar invite. Also can you bring a ballpark for lead times on Dedicated reservation provisioning and a short note on fallbacks (how fast Hosted overflow ramps)?
